target_customer: Health conscious adults and patients wanting brain MRI analysis, via partner MRI centers
problem: People get brain MRIs without accessible, quantified analysis, so brain health and dementia risk are identified late.
business_model: direct to consumer service: about $390 for a brain MRI exam with AI analysis and dashboard (AuntMinnie, 2020)
product_category: AI brain MRI analysis and brain health

founders.name: Owen Phillips
prior_employers: Stanford University School of Medicine (postdoctoral fellow)
founders.background_notes: YC page: Stanford-trained entrepreneur and neuroscientist, PhD. The postdoc detail comes from a profile snippet, not an opened page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Segmenting brain regions from clinical MRI and producing a 3D dashboard and BrainAge score needs neuroimaging expertise plus integration with MRI centers.

defensibility.rationale: Analysis methods are published science; a critical third party review notes no FDA clearance, so there is no regulatory moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents offering a consumer equivalent; consumer MRI firms emerged later.

market_need_then: The founder says he started after his mother's treatable dementia was missed (Foresight talk summary); dementia diagnosis is widely underserved.

branding.domain_note: Now at brainkey.ai; the earlier domain is not documented.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission statement: a world free from dementia

branding.community_and_virality: Trade press (AuntMinnie 2020) and a longevity community review; no merch or fan evidence.

brand_strength.rationale: Name states the product and mission; coverage is limited to niche press and reviews.

pivots.from: Brain MRI analysis for patients and individuals
pivots.to: Brain longevity plus expansion to whole body MRI
pivots.why: Described in later profile text; date and reasoning not sourced.

outcome_analysis: BrainKey, a single founder neuroscience company from YC Winter 2019, sells brain MRI analysis directly to consumers. It is still active with a team the YC page puts at 20, and has added whole body MRI. No priced round, revenue or customer figures were found and a critical review notes no FDA clearance, so the evidence supports survival but not traction or a funding trajectory.
notes: brainkey.ai could not be fetched (domain check rate limited). Seedtable lists a March 2019 seed with five investors but the amount and names were not visible; single aggregator, so no round recorded. Competitors: AuntMinnie 2020 names none and aggregator lookalike lists are undated, so the list is empty. Team size estimates conflict (6, 14, 20).
